title: Tracking the dynamics of single fused synaptic vesicle proteins from a single ribbon active zone in zebrafish retinal bipolar cells
protocol: Add 10 mM glucose to 0.5 and 2.5 mM Ca²⁺HEPES solutions and oxygenate them.
Reconstitute RBP-Cy5 peptide in pipet solution.
Dilute 1.4 μL of the 2.5 mM Cy5-RBP stock with intracellular/pipet solution (100 μL) to a final working concentration of 35 μM.
Load diluted solution into filler pipet.
Wrap loaded filler pipet in aluminum foil and place it in a covered ice box.
Prepare standard pipets for patch-clamp experiments.
Coat the pipets with dental wax or other hydrophobic insulator to decrease stray capacitance and improve noise characteristics.
Melt dental wax in homemade molten supply.
Dip and rotate the pipet in liquid wax to evenly coat the tip.
Turn on the two LED lights in the microforge and set the heat/speed control to ∼6.
Position the pipet so that both it and the platinum heating filament are visible using the 60×/0.6 objective.
Precisely position the pipet tip against the polishing coil using the 10× long working distance plan achromatic objective.
Maintain a distance of ∼75 μm between the pipet tip and the filament.
Control the polishing by pressing the pedal for a count of ∼3.
Store prepared pipets in an air-tight container to prevent dust particles.
Perform a whole-cell recording.
Label the synaptic ribbon.
Secure the glass-bottom dish plated with bipolar cells firmly to the LSCM sample holder.
Select ocular mode to manually search for an intact rod bipolar cell using the 60 X silicon objective lens.
Focus on the cell of interest using differential contrast.
Confirm that the cell is a healthy, intact bipolar cell suitable for the experiment.
Switch from ocular to LSM mode.
Use transmitter-detected channel to focus sharply on the selected bipolar cell soma or terminal.
Prepare an intracellular solution containing 35 μm Cy5-RBP.
Perform a whole-cell patch clamp recording with the intracellular solution.
Use a fire-polished, wax-coated glass pipet with appropriate resistance for the cell type.
Approach the soma or terminal of the selected cell with brief positive pressure applied via mouthpiece.
Focus sharply on the edge of the cell and the tip of the pipet before advancing.
Release the positive pressure when an indentation forms in the plasma membrane.
Secure the mouthpiece to prevent any movements during recording.
Ensure the seal resistance is greater than 3GΩ for a successful whole cell recording.
Wait approximately 2–3 seconds for steady state labeling of synaptic ribbons after establishing the whole-cell configuration.
Use fast scanning to minimize phototoxicity and photobleaching, especially when patching soma or with higher access resistance (>30 mΩ).
Select the dyes used for imaging in the FV 3000 software.
Perform x-y and x-t line scan imaging of a single SypHy molecule at a ribbon location.
Zoom in on the cell terminal using the 60× objective.
Acquire x-y raster scans with a scan speed of 2 μs/pixel (frame size, 256 × 256 pixels).
Monitor global SypHy responses to sustained depolarization.
Stimulate the bipolar cell terminal for 500 ms or 1 second at 30-second intervals during experiments.
Include terminals with leak current <20 pA for analysis.
Use sequence manager in FV 3000 FluoView software.
Generate logic pulses between the PatchMaster and Imaging computers.
Obtain x-y scans before, during, and after the stimulus.
Generate rapid x-t line scans of a specific duration for a zoomed region through a selected ribbon to monitor SypHy fluorescence.
Adjust the focal plane carefully to bring labeled ribbons into sharp focus.
Avoid focusing on the region of high curvature near the top of the terminal.
Avoid focusing on the plane of adherence of the membrane to the glass coverslip at the bottom of the terminal.
Diffuse RBP in the pipette solution into the cells.
Label the ribbon with the diffused RBP.
Measure SypHy fluorescence intensity changes before, during, and after depolarization stimuli.
Deliver a 1-s depolarizing stimulus to the cell.
Assay fluorescence throughout the terminal using confocal optical sections.
Analyze spatially averaged SypHy fluorescence as a function of time.
Fit the fluorescence data to a declining exponential curve.
Use Olympus viewer to open x-t line-scan images.
In ImageJ, average the x-t images over 2 pixels in the x-axis and 5 lines in the t-axis using the Scale command on the Image menu.
Analyze the x-axis profile of the x-t line scan to determine the spatial profile of SypHy fluorescence with respect to the ribbon.
Use the rectangular option in ImageJ to draw a region of interest encompassing the entire line-scan.
Go to Analyze > Plot profile.
If the ribbon profile demonstrates any movement along the time axis and/or bleaching, do not continue the analysis.
Keep the standard orientation for analysis with the outside of the cell on the right-hand side.
For images acquired with the ribbon on the left-hand side, flip both channels horizontally in ImageJ using Image > Transform > Flip Horizontally.
Click the list in the bottom panel of the line profile to view the plot values.
Copy the selected data from the line profile.
Open Igor Pro 8 software and go to Windows > Select New Table > Paste.
In Igor Pro 8, go to Windows > Select New Graph and assign gray values for Y waves and distance as X waves.
Fit x-axis intensity profiles with the equation f(x) = s(x) + g(x).
Use s(x) = b - (c / (1-exp((x1/2-x)/d))) to describe fluorescence transition at cell edges.
Define g(x) = a * exp(-(x-x0)^2/w^2) for RBP and SypHy fluorescence.
Set x1/2 as the position of the plasma membrane on the x-axis.
Set x0 as the x-axis position of the fluorescence emitter.
Identify b as intracellular background fluorescence.
Identify c as extracellular background fluorescence.
Determine d as the slope factor of the sigmoid function.
Define a as the peak amplitude of emitter fluorescence.
Calculate w as √2 * standard deviation of the Gaussian function.
Analyze the time-axis profile of the x-t line scan to determine the temporal profile of SypHy fluorescence with respect to the ribbon.
Obtain the kinetics of the SypHy event using ImageJ and Igor Pro8 software.
Scale the time profile (X axis) with appropriate information.
Reorient the x-t scan as demonstrated in Figure 3C.
Obtain the temporal profile as indicated in Figure 3D.
Define the event amplitude as the difference between baseline amplitude and peak amplitude.
Determine the baseline by averaging fluorescence obtained immediately before depolarization.
Identify the maximum value that occurs early during the SypHy event to measure peak amplitude.
Average 5 points centered around the peak amplitude for measurement.
